newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon, Northrop bid for Hughes.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon, Northrop bid for Hughes.

text.p: Raytheon Corp and Northrop Grumman Corp have both bid $9 billion or more for the missile and defense business of Hughes Electronics Corp, sources familiar with the deal said Thursday.
"Northrop and Raytheon have put in bids," one investment banker familiar with the auction said.
Raytheon is said to have bid $9 billion with Northrop coming in with a bid of up to $9.5 billion, reports said.
"All things being equal I think Raytheon have some advantages," another investment banker close to the deal said.
He said Raytheon has the edge because it has three non-defense businesses that it could sell for as much as $6-7 billion. Northrop has nothing to sell to raise cash.
Both bids were higher than Wall Street or Hughes's expectations, they said.
"Northrop Grumman wants it more but the question is how much they can afford," said the banker. "Raytheon has the stronger balance sheet and the ability to do it, Northrop wants it more."
Neither of the bankers expects the bidding to go much higher, although they couldn't rule it out.
The winning bidder may get a goodwill tax write-off of over $1 billion, reducing the effective price, they said.
Hughes and its parent General Motors Corp, Raytheon and Northrop all declined comment.
